answer: One concrete defense is staked, graph-attested identity. Every agent locks real collateral—a basalt-hard bedrock stake—to mint an identity in the ocean of competing agents. Each identity becomes a vertex in a peer-attested trust graph; positive edges accrue only from distinct honest peers after observed work. To run N sybils, an attacker must lock N stakes and buy N bridges of trust from scarce honest peers, and any detected sybil is slashed with its edges severed. Each fake vertex thus costs real capital plus hard-to-acquire reputation, keeping the attack expensive rather than nearly free.
